To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) visual storytelling is a promising new direction for multimodal media understanding, (2) VQA is a challenging multimodal task that is best approached by harnessing linguistic patterns, and (3) the linguistic patterns latent within language models are also useful for affective content analysis of images.

(1) visual storytelling is a challenging, but important, task that benefits from a synthesis of visual and linguistic patterns; (2) VQA is an important, but challenging, task that also benefits from a synthesis; and (3) linguistic patterns can be leveraged to improve the performance of a task that is, on the surface, unimodal.

(1) visual storytelling can be performed effectively using hierarchical context based networks that leverage co attention mechanisms that jointly attend to patterns in visual and linguistic inputs, and (2) linguistic patterns can be harnessed to improve performance in VQA, and may also be useful in analyzing affective content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
leveraging the rich patterns that exist in the multimodal space, and with developing new models that are capable of learning from and producing multimodal data.
developing novel multimodal approaches to three tasks that have the potential to benefit from the synergistic fusion of linguistic and visual inputs.
developing models that leverage multimodal patterns for a variety of tasks, and we hope that our work can help to bridge the gap between human and machine performance in complex tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first paper that has been written about multimodal media analysis.

the work I have described in this talk has demonstrated that multimodal models can leverage the patterns latent in linguistic and visual input, and in so doing, can perform complex, intelligent tasks that require an integrated analysis of multiple modalities.
the work presented here provides a strong foundation for future multimodal media research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in leveraging the linguistic patterns in text to solve complex multimodal problems.
we have developed novel approaches to three different multimodal tasks, with the common thread that our models exploit the latent structure in linguistic patterns to improve performance.
the use of language patterns is beneficial in a variety of tasks, and that this is particularly true for multimodal tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multimodal patterns can be a powerful resource for a variety of tasks, and can provide an important bridge towards more humanlike machine intelligence.

, while the performance of machines on complex tasks has improved, we still have a long way to go to match humans in their ability to leverage information from a variety of modalities to perform complex tasks.
, in order to achieve truly humanlike performance, machines must be able to effectively leverage patterns in multimodal data.
